Senses.PreferredTarget: a verse on an old case
AlternateTargets: to compose verses on old cases
collection of verses on old cases
Senses.Explanation: A verse composed on an old recorded case, also the named genre, collection, and act of composing such verses. The corpus treats it as a category beside “picking up old cases” (拈古): “there is picking up old cases; there are verses on old cases” (有拈古焉有頌古焉). It counts and titles the resulting works, including “Xuedou's hundred verses on old cases” (雪竇頌古百則), and a collected record says that “one hundred verses on old cases formed a book” (頌古百首為成書). A Book of Serenity preface compares the verses of Xuedou and Tiantong to Li Bai and Du Fu in poetry. Verbal records say that monks “present their understanding and compose verses on old cases” (呈見解，作頌古), that a retired master composed one hundred, and that Dahui composed one hundred and ten while living at Yunmen hermitage. The poems, genre headings, collections, and composition constructions all concern the same literary product and event; noun and verb grammar does not create a second lexical thing.
Senses.Note: The headword has 1,075 hits in 264 allowlisted texts. Headings, numbered sets, anthologies, prefaces, and composition predicates establish one concrete Chan literary genre. The former result/act targets were grammatical views of the same verse and could not be distinguished as different referents from the targets alone. Compare picking up old cases (拈古), old cases (古則), public cases (公案), and appraisal-commentary (評唱).
